newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends mixed, soyoil closes lower.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends mixed, soyoil closes lower.

text.p: CBOT soymeal ended mixed with nearby months supported by gains in July soybean futures, and soyoil ended lower, traders said.
Some pressure in soyoil futures was tied to talk that China cancelled a 28,000-tonne purchase of U.S. soyoil, traders said.
U.S. exporters on Thursday said the deal fell through and the sale was cancelled. Some traders in China agreed, while others said the vessel for the shipment had been fixed.
"The whole thing never made sense to me," a CBOT soyoil trader said. "They (China) have no reason to buy U.S."
Export sales data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture was seen as mildly supportive. USDA net export sales of soyoil of 2,000 tonnes were within the range of expectations for nil to 5,000 tonnes.
Net export sales of old crop soymeal were slightly above expectations at 54,700 tonnes. Expectations had been for 30,000 to 40,000 tonnes.
July soymeal ended up $2.20 at $273.90 per ton, and other months ended $0.60 higher to $2.20 lower. July soyoil settled down 0.03 at $23.04 cent a lb, and other months settled down 0.25 to 0.04.
In soymeal trade, ADM bought 200 lots July and 100 October, and Cargill bought 100 August and 100 July. Term Commodities also bought 200 lots July, pit sources said.
In soyoil trade, ADM bought 100 lots September and Cargill bought 200 August. Term Commodities sold 300 lots July, sources said.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 21,000 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 25,041 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 14,000 lots, against Wednesday's 21,539.
